action-dependency-interactions.reason: the faces of a die depend on no other entry

caller-controlled-sizes.reason: no size or count is caller-controlled here; the step surface has no limit and a caller bounds its own playouts

exception-leakage.reason: Legal paths never throw: every game in the equivalence and terminal tests runs to its end. A bad argument (null, a face no die shows, a play not offered, an index out of range) throws ArgumentException, ArgumentOutOfRangeException or ArgumentNullException by design, as Opening, DiceThrow and Movement already do for programmer errors; it is never a rules decline.

exclusive-or.reason: the corpus sentence behind this entry holds no disjunction that the step surface implements

idempotence.reason: listing the outcomes repeats the same shared immutable table, which P1 reads twice per state

invalid-intermediate-state.reason: no intermediate state is built from a face; an invalid face is refused before one is

missing-content-masking.reason: the step surface reads no optional content, so nothing can be missing and mask a decline

overflow-underflow.reason: the outcome table is built from six faces by constant loops, with no caller arithmetic

phase-state-boundaries.reason: the faces of a die do not depend on a phase of the game

refusal-classification.reason: a face outside one to six is an argument error and never a rules decline

sentinel-wraparound.reason: default(DiceThrow) holds faces 0 and 0, which H3 refuses; no other sentinel exists
